anchors: Record a `rejected` entry for each upstream part Step 3 deliberately left out
decision: Before the adoption commit, record the adoption's decisions in the new skill's ledger with skill_decisions.py add --from-file: a rejected entry for each upstream part deliberately left out, and an anchored rule entry for each house rule added that upstream does not have; the ledger and the checklist naming the ids go in the adoption commit.

evidence.text: Plan M3.5 (2026-11-06). Probes: two opus arms on the pre-edit text named no durable record of a removed upstream section beyond the commit message; with the new text two opus and one haiku arm wrote both entries and ran add, and a control adoption that decided nothing wrote none.

reopen_if: Re-syncing an adopted skill gains its own mechanism that records and enforces the local delta against upstream, or the per-skill ledger is retired.
why: A commit message guards nothing: a later sync from upstream would re-import a removed part and drop an added rule silently. The ledger is what the next editor of the skill is shown (meta-skill-writer Step 0b), and the commit gate refuses a change that drops a live rule anchor.

anchors: The adoption commit and its push are yours
decision: The agent makes the adoption commit and its version bump and pushes it; the adopt_skill.py helper never commits or pushes, and nobody uninstalls anything.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-07: 'Agent commits+pushes' (the agent commits, bumps and pushes the adoption like any other change to this repo; the helper stays read-only)

reopen_if: The marketplace stops shipping changes by direct push (for example it requires pull requests), or the user wants to review adopted third-party text before it is published.
why: The skill listed 'letting yourself commit or push' as a mistake while Step 4 had the agent make the adoption commit; the user ruled that an adoption ships like every other change to this repo, and an unpushed adoption reaches nobody.

anchors: Ship it from the branch, or delete the branch.
decision: The adoption is one commit on its own worktree branch, pushed only once upstream stalls or declines, after bump_version.py --rebase renumbers a version taken meanwhile; if upstream takes the change, the branch is deleted.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-07: 'Branch, push on fallback' (keep upstream-first; push on fallback after re-running the bump; delete the branch if upstream accepts). bump_version.py --rebase was executed on a commit whose version origin had taken: it renumbered it onto origin and refused a second run.

reopen_if: Upstream-first is dropped (the bitranox copy ships at once), or 'stalls' gets a defined time limit that changes when the push happens.
why: Step 4 commits before Step 5 offers the change upstream, so without a rule the commit waited unpushed on a shared checkout, could lose its version number to another release, and had no defined fate when upstream accepted.
